author: TechnoRing Legion Synthesis
description: Production-grade Kubernetes operations skillset for self-managed clusters on ESXi-virtualized infrastructure. Covers containerd v2 CRI lifecycle, CNI networking, storage, backup, RBAC, observability, upgrade procedures, and incident response playbooks. Synthesized from containerd/containerd upstream issues, Kubernetes SIG documentation, VMware vSphere best practices, and production incident taxonomies.
core_principles: CONTAINERD_V2_CONFIG_IS_VERSION_3: containerd 2.x uses config version=3 with plugin IDs prefixed io.containerd.cri.v1.* — not the legacy io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri.* used in containerd 1.x version=2 configs
CRI_PLUGIN_MUST_NOT_BE_DISABLED: disabled_plugins=["cri"] in config.toml is the single most common cause of unknown service runtime.v1.RuntimeService — always check this first

MIRRORS_AND_CONFIG_PATH_ARE_MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE: inline registry.mirrors cannot coexist with config_path in the same plugin block — use one or the other; config_path + hosts.toml is the v2-canonical approach
STALE_SHIM_PROCESSES_BLOCK_CRI: orphaned containerd-shim-runc-v2 processes holding socket state can prevent containerd from cleanly reloading; kill them before restart
ETCD_IS_THE_CLUSTER_BRAIN: etcd snapshot + Velero resource backup are complementary — etcd alone does not preserve PVs; Velero alone does not restore cluster state atomically
CORDON_BEFORE_DRAIN_BEFORE_MAINTENANCE: always cordon first to stop new scheduling, then drain to evict workloads, never skip cordon on short maintenance windows

CNI_MTU_MUST_ACCOUNT_FOR_ENCAPSULATION: VXLAN adds 50 bytes overhead; on ESXi VMs with standard 1500 MTU host NICs, pod MTU must be ≤1450 for VXLAN, ≤1440 for VXLAN+Calico, ≤1420 for WireGuard-encrypted Cilium
ESXI_DISK_ENABLEUUID_IS_MANDATORY: all Kubernetes VMs on vSphere must have disk.EnableUUID=1 set or CSI volume attachment will fail silently
SYSTEMD_CGROUP_DRIVER_MANDATORY: on systemd hosts, both containerd and kubelet must use the systemd cgroup driver — cgroupfs mismatch causes memory pressure OOM kills and pod eviction storms
CONTROL_PLANE_UPGRADES_FIRST: etcd → kube-apiserver → controller-manager → scheduler → worker nodes; never upgrade workers before control plane components

layer_0_containerd_cri_lifecycle.description: containerd v2 CRI plugin loading, config normalization, socket validation, and stale shim recovery

truths: Root cause 1 — disabled_plugins=["cri"]: most common single cause; config.toml created by Docker installation disables the CRI plugin; fix: remove disabled_plugins line and restart containerd

Root cause 2 — mirrors+config_path conflict: containerd v2 raises 'invalid cri image config: mirrors cannot be set when config_path is provided'; manifests as io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri or io.containerd.cri.v1.images plugin failing to load; the CRI runtime plugin then also fails as a cascade because it depends on the image plugin

Root cause 3 — outdated containerd version: Ubuntu 20.04 ships containerd 1.5.x which does not implement CRI v1 RuntimeService for Kubernetes 1.24+; minimum required is containerd 1.6.4+ for k8s 1.24; use Docker's apt repo to get containerd.io 1.6.x+

Root cause 4 — stale shim processes: after hard kill of containerd, orphaned containerd-shim-runc-v2 processes hold the runtime socket references; containerd restart fails to claim them; fix: pkill -f containerd-shim; rm -f /run/containerd/containerd.sock; systemctl restart containerd
Root cause 5 — socket permission: crictl returns 'permission denied' on /run/containerd/containerd.sock when run without sudo or without the user being in the containerd group

Root cause 6 — config version mismatch: mixing version=2 plugin keys (io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri) with version=3 keys (io.containerd.cri.v1.runtime) in the same config causes silent ignoring of blocks and partial plugin loading
Version 3 config is recommended for containerd 2.x; version 2 is still accepted and auto-migrated but migration can produce the mirrors+config_path conflict bug
Plugin ID map v2→v3: io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri → split into io.containerd.cri.v1.runtime AND io.containerd.cri.v1.images
Minimal v3 config for Kubernetes: version=3; [plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.runtime'.containerd.runtimes.runc.options] SystemdCgroup=true
Registry config in v3: [plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'.registry] config_path='/etc/containerd/certs.d' — do NOT also set registry.mirrors inline
Snapshotter in v3: [plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'] snapshotter='overlayfs' — overlayfs requires kernel 4.x+ and is the default on modern distros
Sandbox image in v3: [plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'.pinned_images] sandbox='registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.1'

Transfer Service (containerd v2.1+): CRI image pull now uses Transfer Service by default; configs that include deprecated mirrors/configs/auths trigger automatic fallback to use_local_image_pull=true with a warning log

CONFLICT: having both [plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'.registry.mirrors] AND config_path set causes 'invalid cri image config: mirrors cannot be set when config_path is provided' — CRI image plugin fails to load

RESOLUTION OPTION A — use config_path only (recommended): set config_path='/etc/containerd/certs.d'; create /etc/containerd/certs.d/<registry>/hosts.toml per registry; delete all inline mirrors/configs/auths from config.toml
RESOLUTION OPTION B — use inline mirrors only: remove config_path entirely from registry block; keep inline [registry.mirrors] entries; note this pattern is deprecated since v1.5 and will be removed
hosts.toml structure: [host.'https://mirror.example.com'] capabilities=['pull','resolve']; for insecure registries add skip_verify=true
_default directory: /etc/containerd/certs.d/_default/hosts.toml acts as global fallback mirror for all registries not explicitly listed
Validate resolution: after fixing config, run 'containerd config dump | grep -A5 registry' to confirm output; then 'crictl pull docker.io/library/alpine:latest' to verify image pull works end-to-end
Symptom: containerd restart hangs or fails; ctr plugin ls shows io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri as 'error'; journalctl shows 'failed to connect to containerd' or socket binding failures
Step 1: identify orphaned shims: ps aux | grep containerd-shim
Step 2: kill all shims: pkill -9 -f 'containerd-shim'; wait 2s
Step 3: remove stale socket: rm -f /run/containerd/containerd.sock /run/containerd/containerd-debug.sock
Step 4: optionally clean state dir if corruption suspected: rm -rf /run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task (WARNING: causes running containers to be unmanaged — only on nodes being evacuated)
Step 5: restart containerd: systemctl restart containerd && systemctl status containerd
Step 6: verify CRI: crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock info
Step 7: verify plugin status: ctr plugin ls | grep cri — all cri entries should show 'ok' not 'error'
crictl must have explicit endpoint to avoid deprecated multi-socket scan: create /etc/crictl.yaml with 'runtime-endpoint: unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock'
crictl info — returns RuntimeReady:true and NetworkReady:true when CRI is healthy
crictl ps — lists running containers; failure here after containerd restart indicates kubelet has not reconnected yet
crictl pods — lists pod sandboxes; useful for verifying pause containers are healthy
crictl images — lists pulled images; useful for confirming image service is functional
crictl pull <image> — end-to-end image pull test through the CRI image service
After any containerd config change: systemctl restart containerd; sleep 5; crictl info — the 5s sleep gives containerd time to initialize all plugins before querying

layer_1_esxi_vm_node_configuration.description: VMware ESXi-specific Kubernetes node configuration requirements, performance tuning, and vSphere CSI integration

truths: disk.EnableUUID=1 must be set on every Kubernetes VM — without it, vSphere CSI cannot map VMDK paths to PersistentVolumes; set via: govc vm.change -vm <name> -e disk.enableUUID=1
VMware Tools (open-vm-tools) must be installed and running on all nodes — vSphere requires it for VM lifecycle events and guest heartbeat
VM Hardware Version must be ≥15 for full Kubernetes + CSI compatibility
Use VMware Paravirtual SCSI (PVSCSI) controller for OS and data disks — significantly lower CPU overhead vs LSI Logic; PVSCSI default queue depth is 64 and can be increased for IO-heavy etcd nodes

Memory Reservation: set full memory reservation on control plane VMs especially etcd nodes — without reservation, ESXi balloon driver or memory swapping will cause etcd fsync latency spikes and leader election failures
CPU Reservation: recommended for control plane VMs in overcommitted clusters — etcd and kube-apiserver are latency-sensitive; CPU steal time causes request timeouts
Jumbo frames optional but beneficial: if ESXi vSwitch supports MTU 9000, configuring node NICs for jumbo frames allows CNI to use MTU 8950+ eliminating encapsulation overhead entirely
overlayfs is the default containerd snapshotter and works correctly on VMDK-backed ext4/xfs filesystems on ESXi
d_type (directory type) must be enabled on the underlying filesystem — ext4 and xfs both support d_type by default; older XFS volumes formatted without d_type will cause overlayfs to refuse to load
Verify d_type: xfs_info /var/lib/containerd | grep ftype — must show ftype=1
SSD-backed datastores (vSAN SSD, NVMe-backed iSCSI) are strongly recommended for /var/lib/containerd and /var/lib/kubelet — HDD-backed NFS causes containerd layer extraction and image pull to be slow

etcd data dir (/var/lib/etcd) requires separate fast disk — target <10ms fsync latency; vSAN Stretched or All-Flash tiers recommended; test with: fio --rw=write --ioengine=sync --fdatasync=1 --size=22m --bs=2300 --name=etcd-fsync-test --filename=/var/lib/etcd/test.fio
vSphere CSI requires: Cloud Provider vSphere (CPI) running as DaemonSet; vsphere-cloud-config secret with vCenter credentials; StorageClass referencing csi.vsphere.vmware.com provisioner
StorageClass storagePolicyName maps to vSphere VM Storage Policy — define policy in vCenter then reference it in StorageClass yaml
Dynamic PV provisioning creates VMDK in the datastore specified by the storage policy; PV name = kubernetes-dynamic-pvc-<uuid>.vmdk
Node Anti-Affinity: vSphere CSI v2.x+ supports topologyKey=topology.csi.vsphere.volume/region for rack-aware volume placement
Online volume expansion: supported in vSphere CSI 2.3+ — requires allowVolumeExpansion=true in StorageClass and disk.EnableUUID on all nodes

Detach failures: if a VM is hard-powered off without graceful kubelet shutdown, CSI may leave volumes in 'attached' state on the old node; force-detach: kubectl patch pv <pv-name> -p '{"spec":{"claimRef":null}}' after confirming VM is gone

layer_2_networking_cni.description: CNI selection, MTU configuration, overlay networking on ESXi, and networking troubleshooting

truths: Cilium (eBPF): recommended for new clusters on Linux kernel 5.10+; highest throughput (~28.5 Gbps pod-to-service in benchmarks); kube-proxy replacement; Hubble built-in observability; debugging requires cilium CLI tools not iptables

Calico: production standard for BGP-routed on-prem; supports BGP peering to physical switches eliminating overlay entirely (best performance); also supports VXLAN/IP-in-IP overlay for simpler setups; Typha required for >50 nodes
Flannel: simplest setup; VXLAN only; no NetworkPolicy support; suitable for dev/test; not recommended for production

ESXi overlay recommendation: Cilium VXLAN or Calico VXLAN both work correctly on VMware VMs; Calico BGP requires physical switch BGP peering which is more complex but eliminates double-encapsulation on ESXi overlay networks
Canal = Calico NetworkPolicy + Flannel routing — a hybrid used in RKE2 default configuration
ESXi VM NIC default MTU=1500 (standard Ethernet); VXLAN encapsulation adds 50 bytes overhead; pod MTU must be reduced to avoid fragmentation
MTU formula for VXLAN on standard-MTU ESXi: pod_mtu = host_mtu - 50 = 1450
MTU formula for VXLAN + Calico on standard-MTU ESXi: pod_mtu = 1500 - 50 - 10 (IP) = 1440
MTU formula for Cilium WireGuard encryption on ESXi: pod_mtu = 1500 - 50 - 32 (WireGuard) = 1418, round down to 1420
Jumbo frames (MTU 9000) on ESXi vSwitch eliminates fragmentation entirely; set on vSwitch → portgroup AND guest NIC; then CNI can use 8950+ MTU

Diagnose MTU fragmentation: ping between pods with DF bit and large payload: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- ping -M do -s 1450 <other-pod-ip> — if 1450 passes but traffic drops at normal sizes, MTU fragmentation is the cause
Calico MTU config: apiVersion=operator.tigera.io/v1; kind=Installation; spec.calicoNetwork.mtu=1440
Cilium MTU config: helm upgrade cilium --set tunnel=vxlan --set mtu=1450
Flannel MTU config: ConfigMap kube-flannel-cfg; net-conf.json Backend.MTU=1450

MTU mismatch symptoms: pod-to-pod communication works for small payloads (e.g., curl returns headers) but fails or hangs for large responses (e.g., downloading files, database queries returning large result sets)
Verify node network: kubectl get nodes -o wide — check InternalIP assignments; if node shows no InternalIP the CNI DaemonSet may not be running on that node
Check CNI pods: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep -E 'cilium|calico|flannel' — all must be Running
Cilium status: kubectl -n kube-system exec -ti <cilium-pod> -- cilium status --verbose
Cilium connectivity test: kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cilium/cilium/HEAD/examples/kubernetes/connectivity-check/connectivity-check.yaml
Calico node status: kubectl exec -n kube-system <calico-node-pod> -- calicoctl node status
Check flow logs (Cilium Hubble): kubectl -n kube-system exec -ti <cilium-pod> -- hubble observe --follow
tcpdump on node NIC: tcpdump -i eth0 -nn 'udp port 8472' — VXLAN traffic; 'udp port 4789' — Cilium VXLAN
CoreDNS health: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns; nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local from within a pod
Network Policy debug: kubectl describe networkpolicy <name> -n <ns>; check pod label selectors match; Cilium: cilium policy get

iperf3 cross-node: kubectl run iperf-server --image=networkstatic/iperf3 -- -s; kubectl run iperf-client --image=networkstatic/iperf3 -- -c <server-pod-ip> -t 30 — expected throughput >5Gbps between VMs on same ESXi host, >1Gbps cross-host

layer_3_containerd_stale_state_recovery.description: Full end-to-end recovery procedure for the specific incident pattern: kubelet API timeout → CRI validation failure → containerd bad state → CRI plugin config error → normalization → validation

truths: Phase 1 — kubelet API timeout: kubectl commands return 'Error from server: etcdserver: request timed out' or 'Unable to connect to the server'; root cause is kubelet on node not responding to apiserver healthcheck

Phase 2 — CRI validation failure: kubelet logs show 'validate service connection: CRI v1 runtime API is not implemented for endpoint unix:///var/run/containerd/containerd.sock: rpc error: code=Unimplemented desc=unknown service runtime.v1.RuntimeService' — means containerd CRI plugin is not loaded or is broken
Phase 3 — stale runtime/shim processes: orphaned containerd-shim-runc-v2 processes from previous unclean containerd stop; these hold kernel resources preventing clean containerd restart

Phase 4 — CRI plugin config error: after killing shims and restarting containerd, logs show 'failed to load plugin error=invalid cri image config: mirrors cannot be set when config_path is provided' — this is a config.toml version mismatch issue, specifically a v2→v3 migration artifact

Phase 5 — cascade failure: io.containerd.cri.v1.images fails → io.containerd.podsandbox.controller.v1 fails as dependency → io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri remains in error state → kubelet CRI validation still fails even though containerd process is running
STEP 1 — Isolate node: kubectl cordon <node> — prevent new pod scheduling during recovery
STEP 2 — Check containerd state: systemctl status containerd; journalctl -u containerd --since '10m ago' | grep -E 'error|failed|warn'
STEP 3 — Identify stale shims: ps aux | grep containerd-shim | grep -v grep
STEP 4 — Kill stale shims: pkill -9 -f 'containerd-shim-runc-v2'; sleep 2
STEP 5 — Stop containerd cleanly: systemctl stop containerd
STEP 6 — Remove stale socket: rm -f /run/containerd/containerd.sock
STEP 7 — Backup current config: cp /etc/containerd/config.toml /etc/containerd/config.toml.bak.$(date +%s)

STEP 8 — Normalize config.toml: generate clean v3 default: containerd config default > /tmp/containerd-default.toml; then apply targeted overrides only (SystemdCgroup=true, sandbox image, registry config_path)
STEP 9 — Verify no mirrors+config_path conflict: grep -E 'mirrors|config_path' /etc/containerd/config.toml — if both present, remove inline mirrors block
STEP 10 — Restart containerd: systemctl start containerd; sleep 5
STEP 11 — Verify plugin status: ctr plugin ls | grep -E 'cri|podsandbox' — all should show 'ok'
STEP 12 — Validate CRI: crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock info — should return RuntimeReady:true
STEP 13 — Restart kubelet: systemctl restart kubelet; sleep 10
STEP 14 — Verify node Ready: kubectl get node <node> — should transition from NotReady to Ready within 60s
STEP 15 — Uncordon node: kubectl uncordon <node>
STEP 16 — Verify pods rescheduled: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
Minimal production config.toml for containerd v2 + Kubernetes on systemd host:
version = 3
[plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.runtime'.containerd.runtimes.runc] runtime_type = 'io.containerd.runc.v2'
[plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.runtime'.containerd.runtimes.runc.options] SystemdCgroup = true
[plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'] snapshotter = 'overlayfs'
[plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'.pinned_images] sandbox = 'registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.1'
[plugins.'io.containerd.cri.v1.images'.registry] config_path = '/etc/containerd/certs.d'
DO NOT add registry.mirrors inline when config_path is set — this is the conflict
To use a mirror: create /etc/containerd/certs.d/docker.io/hosts.toml with: server='https://registry-1.docker.io'; [host.'https://your-mirror.example.com'] capabilities=['pull','resolve']

layer_4_backup_and_dr.description: etcd snapshot procedures, Velero backup/restore, and disaster recovery runbooks

truths: etcd is the authoritative Kubernetes state store — losing etcd without backup means full cluster rebuild

Snapshot command: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).db
Verify snapshot: etcdctl snapshot status <file> --write-out=table — shows hash, revision, total keys, total size
Automate with CronJob: schedule every 6h; run with hostNetwork=true on control-plane node; tolerate node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule; upload to S3/MinIO
etcd cluster size: always odd numbers (3 or 5); 3-node tolerates 1 failure; 5-node tolerates 2 failures; never run single-node etcd in production
etcd disk requirement: ≤10ms fsync; HDD-backed storage causes leader election timeouts; benchmark with fio before production deployment

Restore procedure: stop kube-apiserver (remove from /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ on control plane); restore snapshot: etcdctl snapshot restore <file> --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restored; mv /var/lib/etcd /var/lib/etcd-old; mv /var/lib/etcd-restored /var/lib/etcd; restart kube-apiserver
Velero backs up Kubernetes API objects (Deployments, Services, Secrets, ConfigMaps, PVCs) + optionally PV data via Kopia/restic or CSI snapshots
Velero does NOT replace etcd backup — etcd backup captures cluster state atomically; Velero captures Kubernetes resources independently

Install with Helm: helm install velero velero/velero -n velero --create-namespace --set configuration.backupStorageLocation[0].provider=aws --set configuration.backupStorageLocation[0].bucket=<bucket>
Scheduled backup: velero schedule create daily-full --schedule='0 2 * * *' --include-namespaces='*' --ttl 720h
Namespace backup: velero backup create prod-ns-backup --include-namespaces production
Restore: velero restore create --from-backup <backup-name>
CSI snapshot integration: --features=EnableCSI flag on install; requires VolumeSnapshotClass with velero.io/csi-volumesnapshot-class-driver-backup label
Velero on tainted nodes: configure tolerations in values.yaml for nodeAgent DaemonSet to ensure backup runs on nodes with custom taints

Partial restore failure (PVCs missing after etcd restore): manually recreate PVCs referencing existing PVs by setting volumeName in PVC spec or use Velero's include-resources flag to restore only PVC objects

layer_5_node_lifecycle.description: Node cordon/drain/upgrade/replace procedures and kubelet configuration

truths: Cordon marks node unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node> — existing pods continue running; new pods will not be scheduled; check: kubectl get node <node> shows SchedulingDisabled
Drain evicts pods gracefully: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60 -- evicts all pods except DaemonSets; emptyDir data is deleted
Drain flags: --force evicts pods without a controller (standalone pods — data loss risk); --timeout=<duration> sets max wait for pod eviction; --pod-selector to drain only specific pods
PodDisruptionBudget (PDB): kubectl drain will block if evicting a pod would violate a PDB (e.g., would leave 0 available replicas); inspect with kubectl get pdb -A
Uncordon restores scheduling: kubectl uncordon <node> — existing pods do NOT auto-migrate back; only new pods will be scheduled on the node
Post-maintenance verification: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> — verify expected pods re-scheduled after uncordon
Node replacement (ESXi): cordon → drain → power off VM → clone or provision new VM → kubeadm join → uncordon → verify → delete old node object: kubectl delete node <old-name>
Primary kubelet config file: /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml (kubeadm managed); override flags in /etc/default/kubelet or /etc/sysconfig/kubelet
Critical kubelet config: cgroupDriver: systemd — must match containerd SystemdCgroup=true; mismatch causes pod creation failures with cgroup-related errors
KubeletCgroupDriverFromCRI (containerd v2.0+): kubelet can auto-detect cgroup driver from containerd — enable with feature gate to avoid manual synchronization
evictionHard: memory.available<100Mi,nodefs.available<10%,nodefs.inodesFree<5% — default eviction thresholds; lower memory threshold if pods OOMKill before eviction
maxPods: default 110; increase for dense nodes: maxPods=250 requires larger podCIDR allocation in kubeadm config (--pod-network-cidr=/23 or larger)
containerLogMaxSize + containerLogMaxFiles: default 10Mi/5; set to 50Mi/5 for production to prevent log rotation storms
protectKernelDefaults: true — prevents kubelet from modifying kernel parameters; ensure sysctl tuning done via init scripts or DaemonSet before kubelet start
Kubernetes supports skipping no more than 2 minor versions in upgrade — must upgrade sequentially: 1.27 → 1.28 → 1.29
Pre-upgrade checklist: etcd snapshot; Velero backup; review release notes for deprecated APIs; verify all CRDs compatible with new version; check addon compatibility (CNI, ingress, metrics-server)

Control plane upgrade order: etcd (if external) → kube-apiserver → controller-manager → scheduler; on kubeadm clusters this is: kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y on first control plane node, then kubeadm upgrade node on additional control planes
Worker node upgrade: cordon → drain → upgrade kubelet + kubeadm packages → kubeadm upgrade node → systemctl restart kubelet → uncordon
kubeadm upgrade plan: run before applying upgrade — lists version skew issues and required manual steps
Post-upgrade validation: kubectl get componentstatuses; kubectl get nodes; run workload smoke tests; check apiserver audit logs for deprecated API usage

layer_6_observability_and_debugging.description: Diagnostic command corpus, log sources, metrics interpretation, and incident triage patterns

truths: Node overview: kubectl get nodes -o wide — STATUS=Ready is required for workload scheduling; NotReady = kubelet or CRI issue
Component status: kubectl get componentstatuses (deprecated in 1.19+ but still works) or kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep -E 'apiserver|controller|scheduler|etcd'
Event stream (most useful triage tool): kubectl get events -A --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -50 — shows Killing/Failed/BackOff/Pulling events across all namespaces
Pod diagnostics: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> — inspect Events section for OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, Unschedulable reasons
Resource pressure: kubectl top nodes; kubectl top pods -A — requires metrics-server installed

Pending pods analysis: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector status.phase=Pending — follow with kubectl describe pod for each: check 'insufficient cpu/memory', 'no nodes match tolerations', 'Unschedulable'
CrashLoopBackOff: kubectl logs <pod> --previous -n <ns> — shows logs from last terminated container

kube-apiserver: journalctl -u kubelet on control plane OR kubectl -n kube-system logs kube-apiserver-<node>; look for 'etcd cluster is unavailable', 'unable to connect to the server', 'RBAC: access denied'
etcd: kubectl -n kube-system logs etcd-<node>; look for 'rafthttp: failed to process raft message', 'slow fdatasync', 'took too long (>500ms)', 'leader changed'
scheduler: kubectl -n kube-system logs kube-scheduler-<node>; look for 'no available nodes to schedule'; cross-reference with node taints and resource requests
controller-manager: kubectl -n kube-system logs kube-controller-manager-<node>; look for 'cannot attach volume', 'token revoked', 'reconcile loop'
kubelet: journalctl -u kubelet --since '15m ago' -n 200 — richest source for node-level issues; filter: journalctl -u kubelet | grep -E 'error|failed|oom'
containerd: journalctl -u containerd --since '15m ago' — CRI errors, image pull failures, shim crashes
Audit log: /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log (if enabled) — who deleted what when; essential for security incidents
PATTERN: Pods stuck Pending with 'insufficient memory' → node memory requests sum exceeds node capacity even if actual usage is low; fix: right-size resource requests or add nodes
PATTERN: Namespace stuck Terminating → finalizers blocking deletion; fix: kubectl get namespace <ns> -o json | jq '.spec.finalizers=[]' | kubectl replace --raw /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/finalize -f -
PATTERN: PVC stuck Pending → check StorageClass exists; StorageClass provisioner matches deployed CSI driver; CSI node plugin DaemonSet running on target node (check taints)

PATTERN: CoreDNS fails to resolve service names → check pods/services in kube-system; check ConfigMap coredns for forward directive; check UDP 53 is open between nodes; check CoreDNS resource limits (CPU throttling causes DNS timeouts)

PATTERN: Intermittent node NotReady → check network connectivity between nodes; check kubelet lease renewal: kubelet lease in kube-node-lease namespace; check clock skew (>2s causes API auth failures): chronyc tracking

PATTERN: ImagePullBackOff → crictl pull <image> on node to get raw error; common causes: registry auth missing (imagePullSecrets), registry mirror misconfigured, node network issue, image does not exist
PATTERN: OOMKilled → kubectl describe pod shows OOMKilled in ContainerStatuses; check limits vs actual usage with kubectl top; increase memory limit or fix memory leak

PATTERN: etcd leader election storm → high fsync latency on etcd disk; check iowait: iostat -x 1 10; check etcd metrics: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table; add disk IO reservation on ESXi for etcd VMs

PATTERN: API server overwhelmed (CRD reconcile loop) → kubectl get crds | wc -l; check controller logs for tight reconcile loops; scale problem controller to 0: kubectl scale deployment <ctrl> -n <ns> --replicas=0
PATTERN: RBAC access denied → kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> — debug what a SA can/cannot do; kubectl get clusterrolebinding,rolebinding -A | grep <sa>
All pods on a specific node: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
Pods not Running: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector status.phase!=Running
Force delete stuck pod: kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force -n <ns> — use only when node is confirmed gone or pod is truly stuck
Exec into pod: kubectl exec -it <pod> -n <ns> -- /bin/sh
Copy file from pod: kubectl cp <ns>/<pod>:/path/to/file ./local-file
Port forward for debugging: kubectl port-forward <pod> 8080:8080 -n <ns>
Watch pod status: kubectl get pods -w -n <ns>
jsonpath extraction: kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}'
Rollout status: kubectl rollout status deployment/<name> -n <ns>; kubectl rollout history deployment/<name>
Emergency rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns>
Apply with dry-run: kubectl apply -f manifest.yaml --dry-run=server — validates against apiserver without applying
Diff before apply: kubectl diff -f manifest.yaml — shows what would change
Taint inspection: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NodeName:.metadata.name,Taints:.spec.taints[*]

layer_7_security_and_rbac.description: RBAC patterns, secret management, network policies, and pod security

truths: ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding = cluster-wide permissions; Role + RoleBinding = namespace-scoped

Principle of least privilege: every ServiceAccount should have only the minimum required verbs/resources; default SA in each namespace is auto-mounted — disable with automountServiceAccountToken: false in pod spec when not needed
Audit SA permissions: kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>
Aggregated ClusterRoles: admin, edit, view are built-in; bind with RoleBinding to namespace; prefer these over custom roles for standard app access
NEVER bind to cluster-admin ServiceAccount for application workloads — if operator needs wide permissions, create scoped ClusterRole with exact required resources
Impersonation for debugging: kubectl get pods --as=system:serviceaccount:production:app-sa -n production — test what the SA can see without modifying cluster
Kubernetes Secrets are base64 encoded, not encrypted, in etcd by default — enable EncryptionConfiguration for etcd-at-rest encryption: aesgcm or kms provider
Avoid storing secrets in ConfigMaps or plain env vars in YAML committed to git — use sealed-secrets (Bitnami), external-secrets-operator (Vault/AWS SSM), or SOPS

imagePullSecrets: create docker-registry secret: kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=<url> --docker-username=<user> --docker-password=<pass>; reference in pod spec or attach to ServiceAccount

Secret rotation: update secret value; pods do NOT auto-reload env vars from updated secrets — must roll deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name>; volumes: files update within ~60s (kubelet sync interval)
Default deny: create NetworkPolicy with empty podSelector and no ingress/egress rules to block all traffic in a namespace, then add explicit allow policies
Default deny pattern: apiVersion=networking.k8s.io/v1; kind=NetworkPolicy; spec.podSelector={}; spec.policyTypes=[Ingress,Egress] — this denies all unless another policy allows
Allow DNS: any egress NetworkPolicy must allow UDP 53 to kube-dns namespace (kube-system) or CoreDNS will be blocked causing all DNS resolution failures
Allow healthchecks: NodePort services and readiness probes originate from the kubelet IP on the node — if using strict NetworkPolicy, allow ingress from the node CIDR
NetworkPolicy debug with Cilium: kubectl -n kube-system exec -ti <cilium-pod> -- cilium policy trace --src-k8s-pod <ns>/<pod> --dst-k8s-pod <ns>/<pod>

layer_8_storage_and_persistence.description: PV/PVC lifecycle, CSI driver operations, and storage troubleshooting

truths: PVC phases: Pending → Bound → Released (after PVC deletion if PV reclaim policy=Retain) → Deleted (after PV deletion or reclaim policy=Delete)
Orphaned PVs in Released state block new PVC binding to same storage — fix: kubectl patch pv <pv> -p '{"spec":{"claimRef":null}}' to reset to Available, then create new PVC

StorageClass reclaim policy: Delete (default) — PV and underlying disk deleted when PVC deleted; Retain — PV and disk preserved; WaitForFirstConsumer — delays provisioning until pod is scheduled (required for topology-aware provisioning)
Volume expansion: requires allowVolumeExpansion=true in StorageClass; edit PVC spec.resources.requests.storage to new size; CSI will trigger expansion; may require pod restart for filesystem resize
ReadWriteMany (RWX): not supported by most block CSI drivers (vSphere CSI, AWS EBS); use NFS CSI (e.g., nfs-subdir-external-provisioner) or distributed storage (Longhorn, Rook-Ceph CephFS) for RWX
PVC binding debug: kubectl describe pvc <name> — check Events for provisioner errors, topology mismatch, storage policy failure

esxi_k8s_topology.description: Recommended topology for self-managed Kubernetes on ESXi

control_plane_vms.disk_etcd_note: separate VMDK on SSD-backed datastore; measure fsync < 10ms with fio
control_plane_vms.anti_affinity: distribute control plane VMs across ESXi hosts using VM anti-affinity rules

worker_vms.disk_containerd_note: /var/lib/containerd — size based on expected image count; 50-200GB typical
worker_vms.disk_type: VMware Paravirtual SCSI; thick-provisioned eager-zeroed for etcd; thin for worker data

networking.pod_cidr: 10.244.0.0/16 — /24 per node by default supports 254 pods
networking.vswitches: dedicated vSwitch or portgroup for Kubernetes nodes with promiscuous mode OFF (VXLAN does not need it); jumbo frames recommended (MTU 9000) if infrastructure supports

containerd_recovery: ps aux | grep containerd-shim — find orphaned shims
containerd config default > /etc/containerd/config.toml — regenerate clean config
systemctl restart containerd && sleep 5 && ctr plugin ls | grep cri
network_triage: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep -E 'cilium|calico|flannel|coredns'
kubectl -n default exec -it debug-pod -- nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
kubectl -n default exec -it debug-pod -- ping -M do -s 1450 <other-pod-ip>

anti_patterns.cause: Docker installation creates config.toml with CRI disabled; installing containerd from Docker repo alongside Docker leaves this in place
anti_patterns.consequence: unknown service runtime.v1.RuntimeService — Kubernetes cannot use containerd as CRI
anti_patterns.fix: Remove disabled_plugins line; systemctl restart containerd

anti_patterns.pattern: mirrors inline + config_path both set in same registry block
anti_patterns.cause: containerd config migrate from v2 to v3 does not intelligently handle the mutual exclusion; manual config edits adding config_path without removing mirrors
anti_patterns.consequence: CRI image plugin fails to load; cascade failure of all CRI-dependent plugins
anti_patterns.fix: Use one or the other; preferred: config_path + /etc/containerd/certs.d/<registry>/hosts.toml

anti_patterns.pattern: No memory reservation on ESXi control plane VMs
anti_patterns.cause: Default vSphere VM has no memory reservation; other VMs on host can cause ESXi to balloon/swap the control plane VM memory
anti_patterns.consequence: etcd fsync latency spikes → leader election failures → API server timeouts → cluster degradation
anti_patterns.fix: Set 100% memory reservation in vSphere VM settings for all control plane VMs

anti_patterns.pattern: disk.EnableUUID not set on worker nodes
anti_patterns.cause: Cloned VMs from template may not have disk.EnableUUID set if template was not configured
anti_patterns.consequence: vSphere CSI cannot identify VM→disk mapping; PVC attachments silently fail or attach to wrong VM

anti_patterns.pattern: CNI pod MTU not reduced for VXLAN on 1500-MTU host
anti_patterns.cause: Default CNI deployment does not know host MTU; assumes it can use full 1500
anti_patterns.consequence: Fragmentation of large packets; small HTTP requests work but large file transfers or DB queries silently fail or hang
anti_patterns.fix: Set CNI MTU to 1450 (VXLAN) or 1440 (Calico VXLAN) or 1420 (WireGuard)

anti_patterns.pattern: cgroupDriver mismatch between containerd and kubelet
anti_patterns.cause: containerd config has SystemdCgroup=true but kubelet cgroupDriver=cgroupfs or vice versa
anti_patterns.consequence: Pod creation failures; OOM kills occurring at unexpected memory levels; cgroup hierarchy corruption over time
anti_patterns.fix: Ensure both containerd (SystemdCgroup=true) and kubelet (cgroupDriver: systemd) use the same driver

anti_patterns.cause: kubectl drain implicitly cordons but race condition exists; new pods can be scheduled between cordon implicit and drain start
anti_patterns.consequence: Newly scheduled pods immediately evicted; PodDisruptionBudget violations possible
anti_patterns.fix: Always run kubectl cordon <node> explicitly before kubectl drain

anti_patterns.pattern: etcd on HDD or NFS-backed storage
anti_patterns.cause: Cost cutting; NAS-backed datastores assigned for convenience
anti_patterns.consequence: fsync > 100ms triggers etcd leader election storms; cluster instability under write load
anti_patterns.fix: Dedicated SSD-backed VMDK for etcd data dir; validate with fio before production; target <10ms fdatasync

anti_patterns.pattern: Single etcd node for production cluster
anti_patterns.cause: Resource savings; dev cluster config promoted to production
anti_patterns.consequence: Single point of failure; etcd restart causes full cluster unavailability; no quorum recovery option
anti_patterns.fix: Always 3+ etcd nodes in production; distributed across ESXi hosts with anti-affinity rules

anti_patterns.pattern: Using default namespace for all production workloads
anti_patterns.cause: Convenience; beginners starting in default namespace
anti_patterns.consequence: No RBAC isolation; NetworkPolicy scope requires selecting all pods; ResourceQuota cannot be applied per-team
anti_patterns.fix: Dedicated namespace per application or team; RBAC per namespace; ResourceQuota per namespace
